\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Risk cases parseable under both conditions ($n$). Out: trap failure under the first condition only ($b$); in: under the second condition only ($c$). Difference $=(c-b)/n$, the second condition's trap-failure rate minus the first's, in percentage points, with the Newcombe method-10 95\% CI for paired proportions \citep{newcombe1998improved}; $p$: exact two-sided McNemar test \citep{mcnemar1947note}. When $c=0$ the exact test reduces to a sign test on the $b$ discordant pairs, $p=2\cdot0.5^{b}$, a function of $b$ alone.
